name: loglinear_jaganathan
label: Log-linear, Jaganathan 2024 (Indian districts, all-cause, all ages)
source: Jaganathan S, Stafoggia M, Rajiva A, et al. Estimating the effect of annual PM2.5 exposure on mortality in India: a difference-in-differences approach. Lancet Planet Health 2024; 8: e987-96. doi:10.1016/S2542-5196(24)00248-1
locator: Summary (Findings) and Results: 'an increase in annual all-cause mortality rates by 8.6% (6.4-10.8) per 10 µg/m³ PM2.5' (final difference-in-differences model). Floor: the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³, one of the paper's two counterfactuals (Methods, Attributable mortality) and the one behind its 1.5 million deaths a year.

name: loglinear_brown
label: Log-linear, Brown 2022 Million Death Study (non-accidental; studied at ages 15-69, applied from 15, extrapolated above 69)
source: Brown PE, Izawa Y, Balakrishnan K, et al. Mortality associated with ambient PM2.5 exposure in India: results from the Million Death Study. Environ Health Perspect 2022; 130(9): 097004. doi:10.1289/EHP9538
locator: Results: 'all nonaccidental deaths ... [RR 0.99 (95% CI: 0.98, 1.00) vs. 1.01 (95% CI: 1.00, 1.03), respectively]', the spatially adjusted value; Figure 2; ages 15-69, both sexes. Floor: Methods (Statistical Methods), 'PM2.5 exposure in the range of 0-2 µg/m³ ... had no effect on mortality'; the paper computes no attributable deaths.

name: loglinear_vodonos
label: Log-linear, Vodonos 2018 meta-regression (all-age all-cause in the paper, applied from age 25: the pooled studies are adult cohorts), slope at a study mean of 30 µg/m³ (the published slope falls with concentration; one slope misstates it)
source: Vodonos A, Awad YA, Schwartz J. The concentration-response between long-term PM2.5 exposure and mortality; a meta-regression approach. Environ Res 2018; 166: 677-89. doi:10.1016/j.envres.2018.06.021
locator: Section 3 (Results): 'a 1 µg/m³ increase in PM2.5 was associated with a 1.29% increase in all-age all-cause mortality (95%CI 1.09-1.50) at a mean exposure of 10 µg/m³, which decreased to 1.03% (95%CI 0.97-1.11) at ... 15.7 µg/m³ ..., and to 0.82% (95%CI 0.52-1.12) at 30 µg/m³'; Table 2 (inverse transform 1/PM2.5, coefficient 0.071, SE 0.038; all-cause intercept 0.006, SE 0.003). The 30 µg/m³ value is used, the highest concentration the paper prints a slope for. Floor: none published; 5 µg/m³ (WHO guideline) chosen.
